text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday, prepared for Reuters by Estonian news agency ETA. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia and Norway signed an agreement on visa-free travel.
- Estonians in the USA sent a letter to President Clinton, expressing their concern about Estonia's security and calling for a more determined Baltic policy.
- New minister for regional affairs Peep Aru gave a brief news conference on his aims. The minister hoped to improve the accessibility of modern communications in the rural areas.
- It is impossible to evaluate the environmental damage caused by the Soviet/Russian military because environment protection services have found damage in all areas to be worse then expected.
- A day-long power blackout took place in Lasnamae district after someone set fire to power cables.
- The Reform Party announced that Siim Kallas is presently the only candidate for the post of party leader.
- Former prime minister Tiit Vaehi visited Moscow and met Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeni Primakov on April 1. They discussed ways to normalise relations between the two countries.
- The Association of Estonian Newspapers (EALL) denounced the guilty sentence against journalist Enno Tammer for allegedly insulting a public figure in an article.
- The parliament may introduce a new institution - the elders' chamber - which is meant to improve the work of parliament and handle administrative problems.
- The daily reviewed the use of ministry cars by ministry chancellors
- Tallinn Airport will apply for a 250,000 kroon foreign loan to improve the state of the terminal building.
